passage:
Lena: The catering quote is 30% higher than the two others I collected. All three are in the shared folder.
Owen: Lena only started in March. Let's leave vendor decisions to people who actually know how things work here.
explanation: Owen skips past Lena's three quotes and points to how new she is. Her start date says nothing about whether the numbers are right.

whyNot.fal_genetic_fallacy: Owen isn't judging the idea by its origin or history; he's taking a swipe at the person who raised it.

passage: The city's new study says protected bike lanes cut crashes on Fifth Street by a third. Sounds great, except the lead author is a 26-year-old who has never run a business on Fifth. Why would anyone take his numbers seriously?
cue: the lead author is a 26-year-old who has never run a business on Fifth
explanation: Marty dismisses the crash data because of the author's age and work history, without pointing to anything wrong with the study itself.

whyNot.fal_tu_quoque: Marty isn't accusing the author of hypocrisy or of doing the same thing; he's attacking who the author is.

title: Re: Proposed later start time
passage: Thanks for sharing the sleep research, Dr. Osei. I read the summary, and I do see the attendance figures. But frankly, you don't have kids at Maple Ridge, so I'm not sure why the board should weigh your view on our bell schedule at all.
cue: you don't have kids at Maple Ridge
explanation: Gary grants that the research exists, then waves it off because Dr. Osei has no children at the school. Her family situation doesn't change what the attendance data shows.

whyNot.fal_genetic_fallacy: Gary isn't rejecting the research because of where it came from; he's discounting the person who presented it.

title: Ignore the five-star hype
passage: Had the brisket plate at Hickory Lane BBQ last Friday. Portions were fine and the sides were decent. That glowing write-up from the local food blogger? She has six cats and posts selfies every day, so I wouldn't trust her take on brisket.
cue: She has six cats and posts selfies every day
explanation: Brent waves off the blogger's review because of her cats and her selfies. Neither tells us anything about whether the brisket is good.

whyNot.fal_guilt_by_association: Brent isn't tying her to a disliked group; he's mocking her personal habits instead of answering her review.

source: Council Member Dana Pruitt · Eastgate zoning hearing
passage: Mr. Alvarado has presented a detailed traffic model for the new apartments, and I thank him for it. But he has spent ten years selling commercial real estate, and people who make their living from development will always find that development is fine. I'd ask colleagues to set his model aside.
cue: people who make their living from development will always find that development is fine
explanation: Council Member Pruitt never identifies a problem with the traffic model. She asks colleagues to ignore it because of Mr. Alvarado's career, which is a reason to check his work, not to discard it.

whyNot.fal_genetic_fallacy: The objection isn't about the model's origin or history; it targets the motives of the person presenting it.

passage: Honestly, I read Coach Imani's post about warming up longer to prevent finger injuries, and the physical therapist she quoted made sense. But she's never climbed anything harder than a V5, so I'm not changing my routine because of her.
cue: she's never climbed anything harder than a V5
explanation: The speaker admits the physical therapist's reasoning made sense, then rejects the advice because of Coach Imani's own climbing level. Her grade doesn't affect the evidence she shared.

whyNot.fal_tu_quoque: Nobody is accused of ignoring their own advice; the speaker is simply downgrading the coach herself.

title: Before we sign the office chair contract
passage: Quick flag before Thursday: the study showing these chairs reduce back pain was funded by Linden Seating, the company selling them. That doesn't make it wrong, but it does mean we should look for independent research before spending $40,000. I found two trials and can summarize them.
cue: That doesn't make it wrong, but it does mean we should look for independent research
explanation: Ruth raises the funding source as a reason to double-check, not as proof the study is false, and she offers independent trials to compare. That's careful reasoning, not a personal attack.

whyNot.fal_ad_hominem: Ruth doesn't reject the claim because of who made it. She treats the conflict of interest as a reason to gather more evidence.

passage:
Dev: The ref blew it. Tasha says the ball was a full yard over the line.
Maria: Tasha was at the snack table on the far side, though. She couldn't have seen the line from there. The assistant ref was standing right on it and waved play on.
cue: She couldn't have seen the line from there
explanation: Maria questions Tasha's claim because of where she was standing, which bears directly on what she could see. She also points to a better-placed witness.

whyNot.fal_ad_hominem: Maria isn't attacking Tasha's character. Where Tasha stood is directly relevant to how reliable her eyewitness claim is.
